summary: Join our Community Development Theories and Practices Training Course to gain essential skills for fostering community growth and sustainable development.
lede: Community development brings theory and participatory practice together to guide inclusive, locally grounded programs. For community development officers, project managers, local government staff, social workers and grassroots facilitators, the course covers assessing community needs, mapping stakeholders and turning findings into action plans. It also develops skills in inclusive facilitation, mobilizing partnerships, and using monitoring and evaluation to adapt programs and support lasting local ownership.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals committed to driving sustainable community transformation. Whether you're in government, an NGO, or a community-based organization, this training will enhance your ability to mobilize resources, engage stakeholders, and create lasting impact.
audience: Community development officers and field coordinators
Policy makers and local government officials
Anyone passionate about inclusive, sustainable community change
modules: Theories and Models of Community Development
Community Needs Assessment and Stakeholder Analysis
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) in Community Development
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of community development concepts and experience working with communities or in related fields. Proficiency in English and access to a computer with internet are required for participation.
